rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the canonical value-plus-quality combination (BM × profitability, cf. Novy-Marx/QMJ), and swapping raw margin for an industry rank is a cosmetic refinement rather than a new mechanism.

Sales-to-price and margin improvement are each known, but conditioning the sales-yield value signal on a five-year *trend* in operating margin is a genuinely dynamic (not level-based) interaction that is distinct from the standard static value-quality cross, though the 5-year TREND window will cost coverage and reduce turnover-relevant timeliness.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is essentially E/P × (negative accruals) — a mechanical crossing of two of the most heavily published anomalies (earnings yield and Sloan accruals) that has been extensively documented as earnings-quality-screened value.

Beyond being another EV-yield × profitability quality-value rediscovery, the EV denominator can go negative for net-cash firms, which flips the ratio's sign and makes the cheapest-looking names appear expensive (or vice versa) — a construction flaw that will contaminate the extreme sorts.

The INDICATOR gate collapses roughly half the cross-section (all below-industry-profitability firms, cheap and expensive alike) to exactly zero, producing massive ties, a degenerate short leg, and unstable portfolio composition — and the underlying idea is just the same profitability-screened value trade as proposal 1.

Net-cash-to-market is a balance-sheet-composition valuation measure distinct from BM/EY, and gating it on operating profitability gives an economically coherent "cheap operating business that is not burning cash" story with a sign that matches the expression's natural direction.
